newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians warn of explosion in peace process.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians warn of explosion in peace process.

text.p: Palestinian officials said on Saturday that they had decided to send an urgent message to U.S. President Bill Clinton warning of an "explosion" in the peace process which could lead to more confrontations.
"The powers of peace are being rejected and the powers of violence are being pushed forward," said Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, secretary-general of the Palestinian cabinet.

He said the cabinet decided on Friday to send a message to Clinton to "explain the seriousness of the current situation which could lead to confrontations". He did not say how or when the message would be delivered.

Palestinians protesters have clashed with Israeli troops for more than two weeks over construction of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on a hill called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.

"The current situation could lead to a comprehensive explosion resulting from the great Israeli pressures on our people in the security, military, economic and humanitarian spheres," a Palestinian cabinet statement said.
Palestinians insist peace talks can restart only when Israel stops work on the settlement.
But Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is due to meet Clinton in Washington on Monday, has said work on the settlement will continue.

Israel demands the Palestinian Authority crack down on "terrorism" as a condition for negotiating again, charging that it gave a green light for the resumption of suicide bombings by Moslem militants after a year-long lull.
